newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu says Jordan strains are "passing cloud".
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Jordan strains are "passing cloud".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an interview published on Thursday he believed Israel's strained relations with neighbouring Jordan were "just a passing cloud".

Netanyahu, whose policies have alienated Israel's closest Arab ally in recent weeks, told the Jordan Times newspaper he thought the two countries could put their "difficulties...and misunderstandings" behind them.
"Concerns that we heard from Jordan can be seen as a passing cloud and I believe that we can have brighter days ahead," he said. "We've had them before, I'm sure we'll have them again."

Netanyahu's opposition to trading captured land for peace with Arabs and his lengthy delay in implementing an agreed troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron angered Palestinians and the wider Arab world.

Earlier this month King Hussein, who has appeared the closest Arab leader to Israel since his 1994 peace treaty with the Jewish state, asked if Israel was trying to "return to the fortress mentality and arrogant feeling of power".

"Obviously I was sorry to hear of his (King Hussein's) consternation," Netanyahu said. "I think such things happen among the best of friends and I believe that we'll be able to put behind these difficulties...and misunderstandings."

On Tuesday, in a clear demonstration of support for Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat, the king visited Jericho, the first West Bank town to be handed back to Palestinian control under a 1993 self-rule accord.

Netanyahu said he had a dream that one day he could visit Palestinian territories with his children to "meet the children of the Palestinians and have a normal relationship between our two people, our two families".
"Maybe it may appear today a far-fetched dream after the violence that we've experienced," he added.
